newsitem.title: DUBAI: Some 10,000 Kurd refugees arrive in Iran - UNHCR.
newsitem.headline: Some 10,000 Kurd refugees arrive in Iran - UNHCR.

text.p: Some 10,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees fleeing renewed inter-Kurdish fighting in northern Iraq have crossed into Iran to join tens of thousands sheltering there since last month, a United Nations official said on Monday.

"About 10,000 new refugees have crossed into Iran since Saturday, but there are still a lot more on the other side of the border," said Laurens Jolles, an official of the U.N. High Commisioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Tehran.
"Iranian officials estimate 40,000 refugees are waiting at the border, but we have not been able to confirm that figure," Jolles told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
The Iranian news agency IRNA said 7,000 of the new refugees were lodged at two border camps in Iran's Kurdistan province after they arrived on Sunday night.

The new wave of refugees follows recent reversals suffered by the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) -- which many of the refugees support -- in its drive to take back territory lost last month to the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

The KDP tipped the balance of power in its favour in late August by joining with Iraqi troops and tanks to take the main north Iraqi city of Arbil along with most of the region, triggering the first wave of refugees into Iran.
Iran had said some of the refugees, which it put at about 65,000, began returning to Iraq after the PUK regained some of the territory.
Tehran has repeatedly said the refugees faced bleak winter conditions at their mountain camps and held the international community responsible for their plight.
